opinions.rationale: Searched against the 1,376-record screened corpus rather than from memory. Exactly one record addresses the object of this entry: the same 2018 Clinical Epidemiology study the entry cites. The searches that would surface a competing treatment return nothing: zero records for risk set sampling, zero for population comparator, zero for comparator selection, and the only record matching sampling with replacement is that same paper. The adjacent literature is the external control and external comparator work, twelve records, and it is about adjusting a comparison arm to a trial population by weighting or matching, not about the order in which eligible comparators are consumed from a finite pool; the three of those records held in full text contain no occurrence of with replacement, without replacement, chronological order or risk set. The mechanism itself is not novel, since conditioning on the future is Suissa's immortal time bias, but no work applies it to comparator pool depletion or bounds the result. The caveat is on scope rather than on existence. The cited study's own headline is that the three schemes agree in the general population setting and separate only when comparators carry substantial outcome risk, and that the separation largely disappears at one comparator per patient; the entry states this, and a reader should not take the failure as general to matched comparator designs.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No procedure bounds, from quantities available before cohort construction, the bias that the choice among comparator sampling schemes introduces, and the published literature using the design mostly does not report which scheme was used, so the magnitude cannot be recovered from it either.

counter_evidence.title: Sampling strategies for selecting general population comparison cohorts
counter_evidence.what_it_shows: Bounds the scope rather than the problem: at one comparator per index person the three schemes nearly coincide, so the failure is a property of the sampling ratio and comparator risk together rather than of matched comparator designs in general.
counter_evidence.quote: when we sampled one to one, the differences between all comparison cohorts decreased, though the mortality rate was still elevated in the comparison cohort sampled without replacement in random order

counter_evidence.title: Sampling strategies for selecting general population comparison cohorts
counter_evidence.what_it_shows: Supports the reporting half of the entry directly: of the published studies using this design that it surveys, most do not state the sampling strategy at all.
counter_evidence.quote: While a few studies reported sampling with replacement, 5 , 19 the sampling strategy was not described in others.
